newsitem.title: UK: Russia must up gas output to keep mkt share - Gazprom.
newsitem.headline: Russia must up gas output to keep mkt share - Gazprom.

text.p: Russia must increase its natural gas supply by at least 50 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year just to hold its existing share in the European market, Rem Vyakhirev chairman of Russian gas giant Gazprom said on Monday.

Speaking at an industry conference Vyakhirev said last year 18.7 percent of Western European demand was met from Russia "but to develop this further Gazprom must increase output by not less than 50 bcm a year. This is not expansionism, this is just to keep our market share" he said.

He added that gas from the giant fields in the Yamal peninsula would enable Russia to supply Europe well into the next century. He expects Yamal production to start after 2000 and peak at a level of 200 to 250 bcm a year.
Vyakhirev pointed out that gas has survived the economic crisis in Russia well.
"In 1995 oil output was down 41 percent on 1990 levels and coal down by 34 percent but gas production has only fallen by seven percent since 1991" he said.
